answer: Measure what a duplicate costs, then make the protocol charge it. First, publish a replication price per identity: bond, runtime and audit hours. Second, slash the bond when an audit fails and log the slash in public. Third, re-check every claim through a reviewer holding no stake in that identity, so an operator cannot pay its own auditor. The result is arithmetic, not trust, since an operator moving like a falcon still pays bond, runtime and audit per identity, while the cipher that hid a farm was the unaudited gap between bond and machine and every marble in the stack is charged in full.
